best-octopus-go-alternative.html.pre: * All rates pulled 23 September 2026. Octopus Go: GO-FIX-12M-26-09-18. EDF: EDF_EV_FIX_GOELEC_12M_V2_HH (Go Electric 12m v2, on sale since 21 July) and EDF_EV_FIX_GOELEC_18M_V3_HH (Go Electric 18m v3, introduced 23 September 2026). Both EDF tariffs share the same standing charge and the same 6.99p/kWh off-peak rate, but since 23 September the 18-month is about 1.2p/kWh dearer at peak than the 12-month — so it now costs more, ties you in for six months longer and carries a £100 rather than £75 exit fee. On these rates there is no reason to pick it. EDF's 18 September increase lasted five days: both versions it introduced closed on 23 September. The 12-month tariff has gone back to the pre-rise v2, and the 18-month has been replaced by a cheaper v3, so EDF's peak rates and standing charges are now below where they were before that rise. The off-peak rate has stayed at 6.99p throughout. On 18 September 2026 Octopus raised prices too, but in a particular way: they set the new pre-VAT off-peak rate to exactly the old including-VAT rate, in all 14 regions. So from 1 October, when VAT on electricity drops to 0%, you pay the same overnight rate as before the rise — Octopus keeps the VAT cut rather than passing it on. Until 30 September you pay 5% more than you did. Their peak rate is a genuine increase either way, and their standing charge is slightly lower after the cut. All figures include VAT at 5%. Note that VAT on domestic electricity in Great Britain drops from 5% to 0% between 1 October 2026 and 31 March 2027, which will cut every rate here by about 4.8% — suppliers' own quotes may already be shown at 0%. Rates are baked into this page at time of writing — always verify on each supplier's website before switching.
